title: Spindle latency microprofile log — experimental scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick exploratory log for a tiny, focused latency microprofile I called 'spindle' — aim is to capture microsecond-level effects from small changes: sub-token batching, KV prefetch window, and jittered arrival patterns. This is a personal scratchpad: rough numbers, plots-as-text, questions to follow up on.

Hypothesis: a narrow combination of aggressive sub-token batching + prefetch window reduction reduces p95 but can worsen p999 when arrival jitter > 15ms. The spindle profile isolates short streams (prompt length 12-40 tokens, generation 8-24 tokens) typical of chatlets and short completions.

Environment:
- Fleet: 4x A100s (dedicated perf pool, isolated tenant)
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (commit 7f3a2b4), with microbatching enabled
- Model: rwd-open-13b-8k (float16, 4-bit quantized variant Q4_0 for this run)
- Client: synthetic-injector v0.3 (arrival jitter control) on devbox
- Key config knobs varied: sub_token_batching (on/off), prefetch_kv_window (256/128/64 tokens), arrival_jitter (0/10/25ms)

Quick run notes:
- Warmup: 60s of steady 50 qps (zipf-like), then ramp to target for 120s, then steady phase for 300s sampled
- Measurement: token-level latency histogram at worker, p50/p95/p99/p999 at request completion, cpu/gpu-util, kv-cache hit ratio, recovered warm-cache rate
- Sampling: 10k requests per config (approx)

Representative raw table (aggregated):
CONFIG                                      | p50  | p95  | p99  | p999 | KV-hit
sub_batch=on, prefetch=256, jitter=0ms        | 8ms  | 22ms | 36ms | 130ms| 0.91
sub_batch=on, prefetch=128, jitter=10ms      | 9ms  | 24ms | 44ms | 210ms| 0.88
sub_batch=off, prefetch=256, jitter=0ms      | 11ms | 28ms | 52ms | 180ms| 0.84
sub_batch=on, prefetch=64,  jitter=25ms     | 12ms | 35ms | 120ms| 840ms| 0.62

Observations / quick analysis:
- Sub-token batching (on) consistently lowers p50/p95 compared to off for low-jitter runs — expected: better amortization of kernel launch overhead.
- However, when arrival jitter increases (25ms), smaller prefetch windows (64) cause KV miss amplification: p99/p999 explode. Likely because the runtime evicts entries more aggressively when window is small relative to arrival variability.
- The p999 numbers are sensitive to microbursts injected by the generator; adding jitter transforms dozens of 200ms spikes into a long tail at p999.
- KV-hit ratio correlates strongly with tail behavior here; below ~0.7 we start seeing pathological tails.

Quick chart sketch (ASCII sparkline of p99 across prefetch windows at jitter 25ms):
pre=256: ▂▂▃▃▅▅▆▇▇▇
pre=128: ▂▃▃▅▆▆▇▇▇▇
pre=64 : ▆▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇  (much taller, long-tail)

Failure-mode anecdote:
- At iteration ~32 with prefetch=64 and jitter=25ms, observed repeated cache churn: worker logs show frequent KV cache refills (+30% traffic to cache backend), combined with GPU stalls reported at the kernel queue. Suggests the prefetch window is too narrow to amortize cache reuse under jittered arrivals.

Micro-profiling traces (notes):
- Kernel queue lengths spike ~4x during microbursts; observed small GC-like stalls on Python side (cooperative scheduling backpressure) at 100-200ms scale — need better tracing to attribute to Python vs runtime C++ threadpool.
- Sampling callback shows more L2 cache misses in prefetch=64 case (need hardware perf counters to confirm).

Immediate actions / TODOs:
- Re-run targeted prefetch window sweep with hardware counters on (perf counters) to validate L2 miss hypothesis (assign to Miguel).
- Add a run with sub_token_batching=on but with conservative max-batch latency threshold lowered (so we don't overly delay short requests) — check p95/p999 tradeoff (Anya).
- Try a hybrid prefetch strategy: dynamic window that grows on observed arrival jitter > 10ms. Prototype idea: measure 1s sliding stddev of inter-arrival, multiply base window by (1 + k*stddev_ms/10). Cheap heuristic to test.
- File an issue to add per-request KV metadata to traces (so we can correlate misses to tails) — linked: SERV-1293.

Open questions / oddities:
- Why does sub_token_batching=on sometimes increase p999 even in prefetch=256, jitter=0 (small number of runs showed tail bumps). Suspect interaction with overflow queue/backpressure when batch drains hit exactly at token boundaries. Need fine-grained timeline traces.
- Is quantized model variant worsening kernel latencies in the tail? Float16 runs are needed as baseline.

Notes for writeup if this turns into a reproducible experiment:
- Keep plots per-quantization variant, and include KV-hit ratio and microburst count on same axis.
- Suggested release to eng-sre as 'spindle-profile' experiment set so SRE can run on larger fleet.

Last quick checklist before I forget:
- [ ] Perf counters run configured (Miguel)
- [ ] Add per-request KV trace flag behind a toggle (PR stub created) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- [ ] Reproduce float16 baseline
- [ ] Try dynamic prefetch heuristic prototype

Short conclusion draft (one-liner):
- For short-chat workloads, aggressive sub-token batching + moderate prefetch (128-256) gives best p95 but tails are extremely sensitive to arrival jitter; avoid tiny prefetch windows (<100) unless you have strong arrival regularity or additional cache protections.

Any follow-ups: ping Anya/ Miguel / Sasha (SRE) if you run more long tails. Leaving this as a living scratchpad — will refine into a short eng note if we can reproduce L2-miss hypothesis.
